Job Title                                           	Research Fellow 
Job Reference	3880 
Application Closing Date	06/12/2026 
Division, Department	Research Division ,Research Centre for E-Mobility and Clean Growth (ECG) 
Salary	Competitive starting salary range from £38,784 up to £42,254 per annum (dependent upon experience) with the potential to progress. A discretionary range for candidates with exceptional experience can be discussed/considered.
Mode	Fixed Term Until 31/01/2028, Full Time 

 

Our Mission

 

Coventry University is a global Education Group that empowers students and communities to transform their lives and society through teaching, learning, research, and enterprise.

An ambitious and innovative university, our research is designed to have real-world impact on society and tackle global challenges through our 13 challenge-led, interdisciplinary research centres. We enable high performing research teams and future research leaders to thrive and make an impact locally, regionally, nationally, and globally. 

The Role

Coventry University is seeking a motivated and talented Research Fellow to join an industry-led collaborative research project focused on battery intelligence for battery energy storage systems (BESSs). The project will investigate advanced battery testing, modelling, and intelligent state estimation, with an emphasis on physics-guided artificial intelligence (AI).

 

Fully funded by Innovate UK for 12 months starting February 1st 2027, the project brings together academic expertise and industrial requirements to develop and validate innovative approaches to battery performance assessment, condition monitoring, and state estimation. The successful candidate will be based at Coventry University and work closely with two industry partners to address practical challenges in battery characterisation, operational monitoring, and intelligent battery management system (BMS).

 

The role will focus on battery testing and data analysis, battery modelling, and the development and validation of AI-enabled algorithms for estimating battery state of charge (SOC) and state of health (SOH). The successful candidate will contribute to experimental investigations, model development, algorithm implementation, and the validation of research outcomes using laboratory measurements and, where available, real-world operational data.

 

This is an excellent opportunity to undertake applied research at the intersection of battery technologies, artificial intelligence, and energy storage, working directly with industrial partners to translate research advances into practical solutions.

 

 

Qualifications Required

 

PhD in Electrical Engineering, Electronic Engineering, Control Engineering, Computer Science, Energy Systems, Applied Mathematics, or a closely related discipline; or a relevant bachelor's or master's degree combined with equivalent relevant research or industrial experience.

Our Successful Candidate

A highly motivated and experienced Research Fellow with demonstrable expert knowledge and understanding of battery technologies, particularly lithium-ion batteries, BMS, battery performance, or battery ageing. Including experience contributing to the innovation and development of the field.  An Advanced knowledge of research methods and techniques with demonstratable adherence to all regulations, you will have the ability to develop research objectives, projects, and proposals for own and joint research.

 

Research sufficient to write up research and produce excellent, high-quality publications in high profile peer reviewed journals and present at national/international events, you will be committed to working collaboratively on research development, delivery and dissemination including interdisciplinary or cross-disciplinary research, public engagement, and knowledge exchange.

 

We are particularly interested in candidates who can combine physics-based understanding with data-driven and AI techniques to develop robust, accurate, and interpretable battery state-estimation methods. Knowledge of lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries, including their characteristic flat open-circuit voltage regions and voltage hysteresis, would be advantageous.

 

 

The Benefits

 

As a staff member of Coventry University, you will have access to a wide range of industry leading rewards and benefits which includes:

Excellent Employers Pension Contribution
30 days Annual leave plus Bank Holidays
New Holiday Purchase Scheme up to 5 additional days
Life Assurance 4x Salary
BUPA Cash Plan
50% off Tuition Fees for staff dependants
CU Reward Scheme – Discounts across a range of High Street/ Online Retailers
Cycle To Work scheme

 

Our Culture

 

As a global Education Group, equality, diversity, and inclusion are embedded within the fabric of our organisation and are a key focus of our core values. We harness the power and potential of the diverse cultures, backgrounds, abilities, and experiences of our students, colleagues, and partners to create opportunities for all.

 About the Role
 We are seeking to appoint a Research Fellow for an industrial innovation project titled ‘Hybrid Cyber Range for Cyber-Physical Energy Systems’ led by Principal Investigator, Dr. Subhash Lakshminarayana.

 You will join the dynamic team led by Dr Subhash Lakshminarayana ( https://subhashlakshminarayana.myportfolio.com/ ), working on developing cyber-physical resilience enhancement algorithms, AI for power grid optimization and security, and prototype software for cyber-physical energy systems.

 The overall goal of the project is to develop novel risk analysis and resilience enhancement methods for cyber-physical energy systems. Specifically, the project will formulate mathematical risk modelling and resilience metrics and translate these concepts into proof-of-concept software tools and algorithms. These implementations will be evaluated within a hybrid cyber range environment to validate mitigation strategies and strengthen energy infrastructure against evolving cyber threats.

 You will undertake independent and collaborative research and will be expected to write up your research for publication. 
 You will be expected to deal with any management/administration problems that may arise from the project and produce and present regular project reports ensuring that the project objectives and deadlines are met.

 This post is based at the University of Warwick (in the Connected Systems Lab at the School of Engineering,  https://warwick.ac.uk/fac/sci/eng/research/grouplist/connectedsystems/  however the successful candidate will be required to make trips to the project partners, who are based across UK sites.

 This is an excellent opportunity for someone previously researching at the intersection of cyber security and energy systems.

 For details on the experience and skills required, please refer to the job description  ( link here ). 

 About You
 You should have PhD-level training or strong / equivalent work experience at the intersection of cybersecurity and power grids and/or application of machine learning for power grids, and be able to integrate the machine learning backend of the intrusion detection system to real-world setups.

 You will have excellent verbal and written communication skills that enable you to communicate clearly, work effectively with colleagues and external partners, and contribute positively to team and School activities.

 Organised, self-motivated and technically adept, you use IT confidently to prepare papers, presentations and technical documentation. You manage your time well, engage constructively with the wider academic community, and bring an inclusive and professional approach to your work.

 Full details of the skills, knowledge and experience required for this role are in the job description.

 If you have not yet been awarded your PhD but are near submission or have recently submitted your PhD, any offers of employment will be made as Research Assistant on level 5 of the University grade structure. Upon successful award of your PhD and evidence of this fact, you will be promoted to Research Fellow on the first point of the level 6 of the University grade structure.

 Full details of the duties and selection criteria for this role can be found in the vacancy advert on the University of Warwick's jobs pages. You will be routed to this when you click on the 'Apply' button.

About the Role

We are seeking to appoint a Research Fellow for an industrial innovation project titled ‘Hybrid Cyber Range for Cyber-Physical Energy Systems’ led by Principal Investigator, Dr. Subhash Lakshminarayana.

You will join the dynamic team led by Dr Subhash Lakshminarayana (https://subhashlakshminarayana.myportfolio.com/), working on developing cyber-physical resilience enhancement algorithms, AI for power grid optimization and security, and prototype software for cyber-physical energy systems.

Specifically, the project will formulate mathematical risk modelling and resilience metrics and translate these concepts into proof-of-concept software tools and algorithms. These implementations will be evaluated within a hybrid cyber range environment to validate mitigation strategies and strengthen energy infrastructure against evolving cyber threats.

 

You will undertake independent and collaborative research and will be expected to write up your research for publication. 

You will be expected to deal with any management/administration problems that may arise from the project and produce and present regular project reports ensuring that the project objectives and deadlines are met.

 About the role : 

 We are seeking a Research Associate or Research Assistant to provide maternity cover on the IMPACT-SIIP project at Imperial College London.  The project is funded by the Advanced Research and Invention Agency (ARIA) as part of their Sustained Viral Resilience Programme, which aims to develop a new class of broad-spectrum antiviral prophylactics (SIIPs) through modulation of the innate immune system. The IMPACT-SIIP project uses mathematical models to understand the potential effects of these future interventions within individuals, and population-level transmission dynamics, including their impacts on population health and health economic outcomes, in order to design target use cases and inform development. We welcome candidates with experience in within-host mathematical modelling, transmission-dynamic modelling and health economic analysis; you do not need experience in all three areas.

 The position is based in the Centre for Global Infectious Disease Analysis, founded in 2007. The mission of the Centre is to be an international resource and centre of excellence for research and training in the epidemiological analysis and modelling of infectious diseases. The Centre has built upon a world-leading research group in the Department of Infectious Disease Epidemiology at Imperial College London to undertake applied collaborative work with national and international agencies in support of policy planning and response across a wide range of emerging infectious disease threats and global health challenges.

 What you would be doing :

 Your work will be shaped around your experience and project priorities, drawing on within-host modelling, transmission dynamics and health economic evaluation. You will develop and analyse ODE models, synthesise evidence within a Bayesian framework, assess uncertainty and maintain reproducible research code. Working with Dr Lilith Whittles, Dr Alba Halliday and collaborators, you will connect analyses across the project, lead peer-reviewed publications and present regular progress updates to the funder and collaborators.

 What we are looking for :

 Research Associate: a PhD in mathematical biology, epidemiology, applied mathematics, statistics, health economics or a related quantitative discipline, or equivalent research, industrial or commercial experience.

 Research Assistant: a first or master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant quantitative discipline.

 Experience developing and analysing mathematical, computational or statistical models in a relevant biological, epidemiological or health economic context.

 Experience with statistical inference, model calibration or parameter estimation, and programming in R, Python or a comparable scientific language.

 Ability to critically evaluate scientific literature, communicate findings clearly, and work independently and collaboratively in a multidisciplinary team.

 What we can offer you :

 Grow your career: gain access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression.

 As a member of research staff you have 10 development days to use to develop your skills and explore your career prospects

 Further Information 

 Please note that this is a PhD level role but candidates who have not yet been officially awarded will be appointed as a Research Assistant . 

 This post is a full-time, fixed-term contract for 12 months ( maternity cover ).

 The expected start date is 04 th January 2027.

 If you require any further details about the role, please contact: Dr Lilith Whittles at l.whittles@imperial.ac.uk

 An 8 month position is supported by the University of Bath as part of the EPSRC-funded Programme Grant ‘SynHiSel’, a major effort linking membrane researchers at Bath, Manchester, Newcastle, Imperial College, Queen Mary and Edinburgh Universities: www.synhisel.com  

 Chemical separations are critical to almost every aspect of our daily lives, from the energy we use to the medications we take. Separations consume 10-15% of the total energy used in the world, with novel membranes having the potential to make these separations 10x more energy efficient and save millions of tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions. However, commercial membranes do not possess the necessary selectivity to deliver these savings, and novel membrane materials are often non scalable nor sustainable. One post is offered to tackle these challenges: 

 In the 8-month post-doctoral position you will work on the manufacturing of monolayer nanoporous graphene membranes for liquid separations. 

 You will join a multidisciplinary group with expertise in materials, chemistry and process engineering, working with Prof.s John Chew and Davide Mattia, Dr Shiqi Huang in the Department of Chemical Engineering at the University of Bath, UK: https://www.bath.ac.uk/campaigns/membranes-research-expertise/  

 About you 

 You should have a PhD in Chemical Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Material Science or a closely related field and a track-record in membrane fabrication, characterisation and testing. Practical experience in membrane fabrication using graphene or other 2D materials and testing of membranes for liquid separations are highly desirable. Expertise in mathematical modelling is a bonus point. You should also have expertise in advanced characterisation techniques like Raman spectroscopy, AFM, SEM, TEM and XPS. 

 Further Information  

 This role is offered on a full-time (36.5 hours per week) fixed-term basis with an expected duration of 8 months. 

 For informal discussions about the role please contact either:

 Dr Shiqi Huang, sh3292@bath.ac.uk, Prof Davide Mattia, d.mattia@bath.ac.uk, or Prof John Chew, Y.M.Chew@bath.ac.uk  

 We consider ourselves to be a university where difference is celebrated, respected and encouraged. We have an excellent international reputation with staff from over 60 different nations and have made a positive commitment towards gender equity and intersectionality receiving a Silver Athena SWAN award. We truly believe that diversity of experience, perspectives, and backgrounds will lead to a better environment for our employees and students and encourage applications from all genders, backgrounds, and communities, particularly from under-represented groups, and value the positive impact that will have on the university. We are committed to maintaining a safe and secure environment for our students, staff, and community by reinforcing our Safer Recruitment commitment.

 We're very proud to be a signatory of the Armed Forces Covenant . an accredited Disability Confident Leader ; autism friendly university , committed to building disability confidence and supporting disabled staff . 

 What we can offer you  

 We're continually expanding our benefits package to better support you and enhance your experience with us and the below is just an example of some of the many great benefits we offer:

 Generous annual leave allowance with an additional 5 discretionary days so that you can enjoy a positive work life balance

 Generous employer contributory pension schemes

 Cycle to work scheme

 Electric vehicle salary sacrifice scheme

 Staff discount at Team Bath gym

 Staff benefits include discounted postgraduate tuition and language courses, alongside a wide range of personal and professional development opportunities such as apprenticeships, LinkedIn Learning, and more

 Local discounts, including free entry to the Holburne Museum in Bath

 We are recruiting a Research Fellow to study the temperature-dependent performance of photovoltaic modules in the field. The post offers access to a unique outdoor PV testing facility at the University of Southampton.

 The successful candidate will join the EPSRC-funded project "TACOS-PV: Temperature Analysis and Characterisation in Operational Solar PhotoVoltaics" , a collaboration between the Universities of Oxford and Southampton and the National Physical Laboratory (NPL). Temperature effects are the largest source of energy loss in PV systems, yet current models were not developed for today's high-efficiency technologies. TACOS-PV will deliver new measurement methods and models for advanced PV, including TOPCon, heterojunction, tandem and bifacial modules. Industrial and international partners include Lightsource BP, RINA, PV Lighthouse, QEERI, UNSW, Oxford PV and NREL.

 The successful candidate will lead a year-long outdoor measurement campaign across multiple PV technologies. This includes:

 developing high-precision in-situ module temperature measurement

 developing high time-resolution I-V tracing to extract temperature coefficients in the field

 using spectral irradiance data to improve ambient-to-cell temperature and energy yield models

 The candidate will have a strong grounding in photovoltaic systems and a track record of journal publications. Essential experience includes spectroradiometry and instrumentation for irradiance and electrical power measurements , together with strong experimental and data analysis skills. Experience of outdoor PV testing, temperature metrology, energy yield modelling is advantageous.

 This post is suitable for a candidate with a PhD* or equivalent professional qualifications and experience in Electronics and Electrical Engineering or Physics and is available to start from December 2026. The post is for a 24-month fixed term appointment. 

 For additional information/informal enquiries before submitting your application, contact Dr. Tasmiat Rahman ( t.rahman@soton.ac.uk )

An 8 month position is supported by the University of Bath as part of the EPSRC-funded Programme Grant ‘SynHiSel’, a major effort linking membrane researchers at Bath, Manchester, Newcastle, Imperial College, Queen Mary and Edinburgh Universities: www.synhisel.com 

Chemical separations are critical to almost every aspect of our daily lives, from the energy we use to the medications we take. Separations consume 10-15% of the total energy used in the world, with novel membranes having the potential to make these separations 10x more energy efficient and save millions of tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions. However, commercial membranes do not possess the necessary selectivity to deliver these savings, and novel membrane materials are often non scalable nor sustainable. One post is offered to tackle these challenges: 

In the 8-month post-doctoral position you will work on the manufacturing of monolayer nanoporous graphene membranes for liquid separations. 

You will join a multidisciplinary group with expertise in materials, chemistry and process engineering, working with Prof.s John Chew and Davide Mattia, Dr Shiqi Huang in the Department of Chemical Engineering at the University of Bath, UK: https://www.bath.ac.uk/campaigns/membranes-research-expertise/

You should have a PhD in Chemical Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Material Science or a closely related field and a track-record in membrane fabrication, characterisation and testing. Practical experience in membrane fabrication using graphene or other 2D materials and testing of membranes for liquid separations are highly desirable. Expertise in mathematical modelling is a bonus point. You should also have expertise in advanced characterisation techniques like Raman spectroscopy, AFM, SEM, TEM and XPS.

 About the role 

 How does the invisible work of managing household and family life shape who participates in politics?

 We are seeking a Postdoctoral Research Associate to help develop a new programme of research on the domestic mental load, gender inequality and democratic participation. You will join the Department of Politics, Languages & International Studies at the University of Bath, working with Dr Ana Catalano Weeks on the UKRI Future Leaders Fellowship project, Invisible Burdens, Visible Gaps: The Mental Load and Gendered Citizenship .

 The domestic mental load involves anticipating needs, planning and coordinating everyday family life. Women undertake a disproportionate share of this work, yet its consequences for political engagement remain poorly understood. Through research in Brazil, Iceland, Italy, Japan and the UK, the project investigates how household responsibilities, gender norms and policy environments shape the mental space available for political life.

 Joining at the outset, you will have an opportunity to shape the project’s qualitative research and help develop new explanations of the relationship between private life and democratic inclusion. Working closely with the principal investigator and researchers in the five countries, you will:

 Help develop and refine semi-structured interview guides and creative visual methods, including participant-generated photographs (Photovoice).

 Support cross-national data collection and collaboration with locally based researchers.

 Lead thematic coding and analysis of interview and visual data, contributing to the project’s theoretical framework.

 Develop academic publications and conference presentations, and contribute to public engagement activities.

 This is an opportunity to combine substantive research leadership with close collaboration and mentoring. You will be supported to develop both collaborative and independently authored publications arising from the project, build international research relationships, and strengthen your skills in research methods and public engagement.

 About you 

 We welcome applicants from across the social sciences. You will bring:

 A PhD in political science, sociology, social policy, public policy, economics or a related discipline.

 Strong qualitative research skills, including experience of interviewing and systematic coding and analysis.

 An interest in gender inequalities, household labour, political engagement or related questions, and the ability to connect empirical findings to theoretical debates.

 The ability to take responsibility for research tasks while working collaboratively with colleagues across countries.

 Strong written and spoken English, organisational skills, and a thoughtful approach to research ethics and participant confidentiality.

 Experience of comparative research, creative visual methods or qualitative analysis software such as NVivo would be an advantage. 

 We welcome candidates whose expertise brings a fresh perspective to the project; prior research specifically on the mental load is not required.

 Additional information 

 The position is full-time and fixed-term for 24 months, with scope for hybrid working. Working arrangements will be agreed with the principal investigator, balancing flexibility with in-person collaboration, participation in the department’s research community, and project activities.

 As a member of Research Staff at the University of Bath, you will be encouraged to take up a minimum of 10 days professional development pro rata per year.

 A lower grade offer may be made (Grade 6) with comparable reduction in responsibilities and amendment in job title to Research Assistant, if a suitable applicant cannot be found to fill the Grade 7 position. Applicants will need to be within six months of their course completion date and will be promoted to Research Associate once their PhD has been awarded.

We seek a Physicist / Physical Chemist / Materials Scientist with expertise in the fabrication and optimisation of perovskite light emitting diodes (LEDs).  This project is funded by the Leverhulme Foundation and is fundamental in nature. The aim of the research is to develop optical structures based on perovskite materials that are able to undergo optical amplification, and lasing. In particular, we wish to develop devices that (i) realise electrically-pumped condensation and optical gain in perovskite microcavities, and (ii) to generate optical-solitons (non-dispersive wavepackets) in perovskite waveguides and ring resonators, using laser excitation. 

 

Your role will be to synthesize and characterise high quality 2D and 3D perovskite thin films – for example CsPbBr3 or PEA2PbI4, which you will engineer into light-emitting resonant cavity diode (RCLED) devices. You will characterise the optical properties of structures you make using CW spectroscopy, with emission also measured following electrical excitation. In a parallel strand, you will also use nanopatterning and other lithography techniques to fabricate optical waveguide structures in perovskite thin films. Experience in the development of perovskite light emitting devices is therefore critical for this role. You will collaborate very closely with a second postdoctoral researcher who will perform ultra-fast spectroscopic measurements on the materials, devices and photonic structures that you will develop.

 

The project is run by Prof David Lidzey, and involves both inorganic and organic ultra-fast spectroscopists (Prof Dima Krizhanovskii and Prof Jenny Clark), and materials chemist Dr Alex Ramadan. Experience in the fabrication and testing of ultra-high brightness perovskite LEDs will be critical for this role. You will need to be able to synthesise the perovskite materials you make and then characterise their structural and optoelectronic properties. Experience of the development of photonic devices, optical-gratings and photonic-waveguides, or optical modelling approaches using transfer matrix models or FTDT approaches is also desirable.

Design, develop and refine experiments in order to obtain reliable data.

Carry out experimental research, including the use of chemicals and solvents.

Fabricate and characterise 2D and 3D perovskite films using structural and optical tools. 

Fabricate high-brightness resonant cavity light emitting diodes and characterise their emission.

Develop processes to perform micro and nanolithography of perovskite thin films, and characterise the structure of the patterned photonic devices.

Prepare papers for journals/presentations either in-house or at national/international conferences or seminars to disseminate research findings. 

Write progress reports and present work at project meetings.

Read academic papers, journals and textbooks and attend conferences to keep abreast of developments.

Plan for specific aspects of research programmes.

If given a particular hypothesis to examine, plan for your own contribution up to 3 months ahead, incorporating issues such as the availability of resources, deadlines, project milestones and overall research aims. Design individual experiments weekly.

Interact effectively with other members of the project team, sharing data and expertise and working together to reach project objectives.

Supervise research team/activities if required.

Continuously monitor and check results. The unpredictability of research means that daily planning is required to accommodate new developments.

Plan several months in advance to meet deadlines for journal publications and to prepare presentations and papers for conferences.

As a member of staff you will be encouraged to make ethical decisions in your role, embedding the University sustainability strategy into your working activities wherever possible.

Carry out other duties, commensurate with the grade and remit of the post

The University of Sheffield is a remarkable place to work. Our people are at the heart of everything we do. Their diverse backgrounds, abilities and beliefs make Sheffield a world-class university.

We offer a fantastic range of benefits including a highly competitive annual leave entitlement (with the ability to purchase more), a generous pensions scheme, flexible working opportunities, a commitment to your development and wellbeing, a wide range of retail discounts, and much more. Find out more about our benefits (opens in a new window) and join us to become part of something special.

 

Overview

 

We have a rewarding opportunity in the School of Electrical and Electronic Engineering for someone with a passion for Engineering excellence, looking to use their skills and experience in Microelectronics to make a significant impact to the UK’s ability to integrate a wide range of electronic circuits to produce complex system architectures.

 

The University of Sheffield is leading a key national “Innovation Knowledge Centre” that will develop Heterogeneous Integration techniques for complex system architectures using different types of microelectronic circuits such as Optoelectronics, Quantum, Radio devices, etc. whilst ensuring secure communication and secure systems architecture. Our Centre for Heterogeneous Integration of Microelectronic and Semiconductor Systems (CHIMES) is aligned with the UK’s Modern Industrial Strategy alongside the UK National Semiconductor Strategy. Our shared goal is to build a sustainable national capability in the Design of Heterogeneous Integrated Microelectronic and Semiconductor Systems.

 

You will join a warm, highly collaborative and diverse academic department where your skills and insights will enrich our research community.  As an engineer you will work with, and alongside, research staff within the department, generating new and novel integration solutions. You will also build meaningful professional relationships with other world-leading UK Universities (Sheffield, Southampton, Manchester, Kings College, Oxford, Cambridge, Queen’s Belfast, Newcastle, Edinburgh, Strathclyde) and Commercial Collaborators to provide the best possible solutions for a wide range of Heterogeneous Integration needs.

 

As this role embraces a broad understanding of system architectures, it offers a supportive environment to continuously learn, grow your skill set and develop expertise in different types of microelectronic circuits and integration techniques.

 

Main duties and responsibilities

 

Collaborate on meaningful engineering projects, both independently and alongside team members within the University of Sheffield CHIMES community.
Continuously build your knowledge to explore Heterogeneous Integration technology, learn standard techniques and solve specific integration requirements and connectivity problems.
Support colleagues in gathering, interpreting and understanding engineering data, working together to reach insightful conclusions.
Propose and implement improvements to current team workflows and methodologies.
Plan short-term projects within your focus area and contribute constructively to broader team goals.
Manage your daily engineering and administrative activities with ongoing guidance, support and access to the necessary laboratory, workshop and research resources.
Connect and communicate openly (orally, in writing and digitally) with Sheffield teammates, IKC partners and external stakeholders, including sharing technical insights through clear reports and engaging presentations.
Participate in inclusive, shared decision-making with colleagues across engineering and research initiatives.
Connect with team members, the Engineering Director and the wider CHIMES community through regular meetings, as well as representation at conferences and industry events.
Maintain a thoughtful awareness of safety within the workplace, fostering a secure environment for yourself and your peers.
Carry out other duties, commensurate with the grade and remit of the post.

The role

We are seeking to appoint a highly skilled qualitative researcher from a social science, health or social care research background with an interest in research with people with learning disabilities. The successful candidate will work on a NIHR-funded study to develop and test an intervention to enhance social care staff capability to promote healthy weight among people with learning disabilities. The post-holder will conduct qualitative research, co-design intervention components with people with learning disabilities and paid and unpaid carers and contribute to the development and preliminary testing of a novel intervention.

This project is led by Dr Karen Coulman as part of an NIHR post-doctoral fellowship award in collaboration with the Bristol Trials Centre and a wider mentorship team from the Norah Fry Centre for Disability Studies (School for Policy Studies), the University of the West of England, Leeds Beckett University, Learning Disability England, Gloucestershire Health and Care NHS Foundation Trust, and the West of England Health Innovation Network.

The post will be situated within the Health Economics and Health Policy (HEHP@Bristol) research group within Population Health Sciences, Bristol Medical School.

The post is available at 80% FTE (4 days per week), starting ideally in March 2027 with funding available until 30/11/2030.

Hybrid working is available. The successful candidate will be expected to work flexibly across the University of Bristol and research sites. Opportunities for remote working will be available where study activities permit and may vary across different phases of the project.

What will you be doing?

You will undertake qualitative research to understand how social care staff can be better supported to promote healthy weight among people with learning disabilities. This will involve working directly with people with learning disabilities, paid carers, family carers, health professionals and policymakers to explore current practice, identify barriers and facilitators to behaviour change, and inform intervention development.

You will carry out observations, interviews, focus groups, creative qualitative methods and co-design workshops, contributing to all stages of the research process from participant recruitment and data collection through to analysis, interpretation and dissemination. Working collaboratively with Project Partnership Groups, you will develop accessible research and intervention materials and contribute to the design, refinement and feasibility testing of a novel intervention to improve care staff capability to promote healthy weight among people with learning disabilities.

You should apply if

You have experience of undertaking and completing qualitative research projects in applied health, social care or public health settings, including the use of qualitative methods for data collection and analysis. You will have a strong understanding of qualitative methodologies and experience of analysing qualitative datasets, including the use of qualitative data analysis software such as NVivo.
You will have experience of leading a research project, or a substantial component of a project, and of developing research protocols and supporting research governance and ethics processes. You should be able to work effectively both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team, building productive relationships with researchers, public contributors, service users, carers and other stakeholders.
We are particularly interested in applicants with experience of, or a strong interest in, conducting research with people with learning disabilities and/or other groups who may experience communication, cognitive or accessibility barriers.
Experience of co-production, participatory research methods, intervention development, implementation research, or the development of accessible research materials would be advantageous.

Additional information

Contract type: Open-ended with funding, ideally between 01/03/27 - 30/11/2030

Work pattern: Part-time/ 80% FTE

This advert will close at 23:59 UK time on 18/11/2026

For informal queries please contact: Dr Karen Coulman (Associate Professor in Obesity Research and Practice), 0117 455 7944, karen.coulman@bristol.ac.uk

 About the role 

 The post arises from a collaboration funded by the ERC Advanced grant “Light interaction with synthetically moving metamaterials - LUMINOUS” and the UKRI Programme Grant “Next Generation Metamaterials: exploiting four dimensions – META4D” with the objective of advancing our understanding of temporal metamaterials and materials with synthetic motion. The successful applicant will be expected to work with Professor Riccardo Sapienza in London and our experimental collaborators to develop experiments in the field of metamaterials and perform advanced temporal spectroscopy of dispersive time-varying metamaterials.

 You will carry out research programmes in photonic metamaterials, nanophotonics, ultrafast spectroscopy and time-resolved measurements, undertake project management and/or supervise multi-disciplinary teams.  We are looking for expertise in experimental spectroscopy and in particular time-resolved measurement of ultrafast light.

 What you will be doing 

 This role is mostly experimental with some theory aspects. You will design and implement advanced time-resolved experiments involving home-built ultrafast laser spectroscopy, and will manage a 10 fs laser setup and generate structural light from it.

 You will work collaboratively within the team at Imperial College.

 What we are looking for 

 You will hold a PhD in Physics (or a closely related quantitative discipline) and have an outstanding record of research achievement. We are particularly interested in candidates with exceptional experimental skills, demonstrated through the development of novel time-resolved measurements with fs resolution, advanced data-analysis methodologies, and experience with time-varying metamaterials.

 The ideal candidate will be intellectually ambitious, highly self-motivated and excited by the prospect of working at the boundary between metamaterials and ultrafast laser physics.

 What we can offer you 

 The opportunity to contribute to a pioneering research programme aimed at establishing synthetic motion as a new paradigm for spatio-temporal metamaterials.

 Collaboration within a multidisciplinary team involving experimental and theoretical physicists.

 Involvement in publications, conference presentations and future grant applications.

 The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and contribute to our mission of “Science for Humanity”.

 Access to Imperial’s sector-leading career support for researchers, as well as opportunities for promotion and progression.

 A sector-leading salary and remuneration package, including 43 days’ leave per year and generous pension schemes.

 A diverse, inclusive and collaborative working culture, with staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing.

 Further information 

 This is a full-time (35 hours per week), fixed-term role based at our South Kensington Campus.

About the role
We are seeking a Clinical Research Fellow to join the University of Leicester’s Division of Respiratory Sciences and undertake a research project investigating potential biomarkers of airway hyperresponsiveness in people with asthma. Funded by the Midlands Asthma and Allergy Research Association, this collaborative project brings together expertise from Respiratory Sciences and Genome Biology. Based at Glenfield Hospital, you will work within the NIHR Leicester Biomedical Research Centre asthma service and will be supported to apply for a higher degree. 

You will be responsible for screening, recruiting and sampling research participants before and after methacholine challenge, supporting the processing and recording of samples and study data, and contributing to laboratory studies using omics methods. Working collaboratively with clinical and non-clinical colleagues, you will analyse and present findings, prepare reports and scientific manuscripts, help coordinate the study in accordance with research governance and ethical requirements, and support the clinical care of participants. You may also contribute to relevant outpatient clinics, supervise junior colleagues and present the research at national and international meetings.

About you

You will hold an MB BS or equivalent, have full GMC registration and a licence to practise, and hold MRCP (UK) or an equivalent qualification. You will have completed at least two full years of Foundation training or equivalent and have experience of working in Respiratory Medicine. You will understand the governance, ethical and data-protection requirements associated with clinical research and hold, or be able to obtain, Good Clinical Practice certification. A demonstrable commitment to research through publications, conference presentations, prizes or academic training is also essential. 

With excellent written and verbal communication skills, you will be able to work accurately, organise competing priorities and manage your workload independently while contributing effectively to a multidisciplinary research team. You will bring an ethical and reliable approach, flexibility, initiative and a desire to learn. Experience of managing patients with asthma, research or statistical methodology, data-analysis tools, or asthma-related research would be advantageous. 

Additional information
Informal enquiries are welcome and should be made to Prof Dominick Shaw on des21@le.ac.uk
 

As part of the University’s ongoing commitment to professional development, this role will also be considered on a seconded basis for existing staff members. Please ensure this is discussed with your line manager prior to applying. More information regarding secondments can be found here.

 The University of Leicester has been changing the world, and changing people’s lives, for 100 years. When you join us, you’ll become part of a community of Citizens of Change, which includes not only our staff and our current students but also thousands of Leicester graduates around the world.
 
As a diverse and forward-thinking employer, we embed the principles of equity, diversity and inclusion into everything we do. That includes not just our core missions of teaching and research, but also our support for staff, students and our local community through our values of Inspiring, Impactful and Inclusive.
 
We’re committed to the wellbeing of all our staff and to the sustainability of our environment, on our campus and beyond. We offer a competitive salary package, excellent pension scheme and a generous annual leave allowance, along with opportunities to develop your career in a supportive and collaborative environment.

You will collaborate closely with researchers from across the University of Nottingham’s Centre for Sustainable Agricultural Systems and the Food Systems Institute, bringing together interdisciplinary expertise to deliver impactful solutions across the agri-food chain.

This post offers an excellent opportunity to expand your technical expertise, develop new skills, and grow your professional networks while making a tangible impact on sustainable agriculture. The University of Sheffield is a remarkable place to work. Our people are at the heart of everything we do. Their diverse backgrounds, abilities and beliefs make Sheffield a world-class university.

We offer a fantastic range of benefits including a highly competitive annual leave entitlement (with the ability to purchase more), a generous pensions scheme, flexible working opportunities, a commitment to your development and wellbeing, a wide range of retail discounts, and much more. Find out more about our benefits (opens in a new window) and join us to become part of something special.

 

The School of Mathematical and Physical Sciences is seeking to appoint a Research Associate in Theoretical Cosmology. This post is funded by the Royal Society through Dr Eleonora Di Valentino’s Dorothy Hodgkin Fellowship renewal for the project “H0 Tension Test” (H0TTEST) and is fixed term for 12 months.

 

The project investigates whether tensions in cosmological observations, particularly the Hubble constant tension, arise from unaccounted-for systematic effects or indicate new physics beyond the standard ΛCDM model. It combines theoretical modelling, cosmological data analysis and numerical methods to explore extensions involving dark energy, dark matter, neutrino physics, inflation and modified gravity. You will contribute to testing cosmological models with current observations and assessing their predictions for forthcoming surveys, with scope to develop research directions that reflect your expertise and interests within the project’s aims.

 

You will work with Dr Eleonora Di Valentino within the Cosmology, Relativity and Gravitation group, which comprises five academic staff (Dr Eleonora Di Valentino, Dr Sam Dolan, Dr Steffen Gielen, Professor Carsten van de Bruck and Professor Elizabeth Winstanley) and six PhD students. The group’s expertise spans cosmology, gravitation and mathematical physics, with an active seminar programme and close links to colleagues in statistics and astrophysics, providing a stimulating environment to develop your research career. Funds will be available to support professional development, including participation in conferences, collaboration meetings and research visits.

 

You should have a PhD in physics, astronomy, cosmology or a closely related discipline, or equivalent experience. We welcome candidates with a strong research background in cosmology and expertise in one or more of the following: cosmological data analysis, statistical inference, theoretical modelling or numerical simulations. We are looking for evidence of research achievement and potential, strong computational and analytical skills, and the ability to develop independent ideas and work collaboratively.

 

Main duties and responsibilities

Contribute to and support the work of the research group (e.g. by giving and attending local working seminars and participating in collaborations).

Prepare high-quality research publications.

Prepare papers for journals / presentations either in-house or at national/international conferences to disseminate research findings.

 Attend international conferences, and give talks on the work of the research group.

Read academic papers, journals and text books to keep abreast of developments and use this information to brief colleagues and inform the work of the project.

This is not a teaching role, however teaching experience may be available if the successful candidate is interested in gaining some teaching experience. This will be dependent upon opportunities being available within the department.

As a member of staff you will be encouraged to make ethical decisions in your role, embedding the University sustainability strategy into your working activities wherever possible.

The Department of Politics and International Relations is inviting applications for a position as Research Fellow to conduct research as part of the ESRC-funded project, The International Politics of Soldier Exchanges: Military Families, States and International Institutions.

Job Description

The Department of Politics and International Relations is inviting applications for a position as Research Fellow to conduct research as part of the ESRC-funded project, The International Politics of Soldier Exchanges: Military Families, States and International Institutions.

The Research Fellow will work closely with Project Co-Lead Dr Natasha Danilova on analysing documents, media and social media coverage pertinent to humanitarian soldier exchanges, and experiences of military families in Russia, using available policy-framing documents, media and social media data sourced from the Integrum database and other relevant sources. Tasks include participating in the creation of a dataset of policy documents that govern the reporting on missing and killed soldiers in Russia; contributing to the analysis of the media coverage of military families across traditional and digital media, including soldiers’ mothers and wives’ protests, and take a lead in the mixed-method analysis of Russia’s military families’ organising on social media and via other digital means.

The Research Fellow will co-author relevant research outputs, participate in the training of the project’s staff, and have an opportunity to present preliminary project findings at relevant workshops and conferences.

The successful candidate will have advanced knowledge and skills in mixed-method, computational/qualitative content analysis (inc. social media data) with expertise on Russia’s politics, gender, war, security and society-military relations. They will be comfortable working across policy documents, traditional mass media, and social media sources, and interested in themes such as military families, gender and feminist analysis of conflicts and conflict-mediation, peace work, humanitarian exchanges, and state-society relations in highly militarized autocratic states.

This postdoctoral position requires a doctoral degree (or a thesis submitted and awaiting examination) in Politics, International Relations, Peace and Conflict Mediation Studies, Russian Studies, History, or a closely related discipline. The successful candidate will be expected to demonstrate a high level of proficiency in the Russian language.

Salary will be at the appropriate point on the Grade 6 scale, £39,560 - £40,704 per annum, and negotiable with placement according to qualifications and experience.

This is a full-time post for 18 months, 1 December 2026 – 31 May 2028.

About us:

The department of Neuroimaging at King's College London (KCL) is an internationally renowned centre focused on advancing our understanding of the human brain and its function using cutting-edge imaging and digital assessment technologies. The department is dedicated to exploring the mechanisms of neurological and psychiatric disorders across the lifespan. It employs a multidisciplinary approach, combining expertise in imaging techniques, computational neuroscience, basic and clinical research.

About the role:

This is an exciting opportunity for a research associate to contribute to research investigating neurological resilience, after an inflammatory challenge, in individuals with familial risk of multiple sclerosis (MS). The post holder will be based in the Department of Neuroimaging at the at the Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology and Neuroscience (IoPPN), one of the most esteemed clinical research centres worldwide, working under the guidance of Prof Adam Hampshire (Centre for Neuroimaging Sciences, IoPPN).

The successful candidate will contribute to a programme of research using cognitive, neuroimaging and immune measures to investigate individual differences in response to transient inflammation. The role will involve supporting participant engagement and recruitment, coordinating research assessments, analysing existing cognitive and MRI datasets and contributing to the collection and analysis of longitudinal data before and after routine influenza vaccination/inflammatory challenge. The role will involve communicating study information and risk to participants and families. The post holder will work closely with researchers across the group and contribute to data management, statistical analysis, research presentations and preparation of publications.

This is a full-time post (35 hours per week), and you will be offered a 6 month fixed term contract.

Research staff at King’s are entitled to at least 10 days per year (pro-rata) for professional development. This entitlement, from the Concordat to Support the Career Development of Researchers, applies to Postdocs, Research Assistants, Research and Teaching Technicians, Teaching Fellows and AEP equivalent up to and including grade 7. Visit the  Centre for Research Staff Development for more information.

Essential criteria

BSc (or equivalent) in Medical Biosciences, Biomedical Sciences or Neurosciences.
Practical laboratory research experience in a research project involving multiple sclerosis, with understanding of multiple sclerosis pathology, disease mechanisms or clinical research.
Demonstrate experience with molecular and cellular laboratory techniques, including Western blotting, qPCR, Proteomics, Flow cytometry, Tissue Culture, IHC/IF and Spatial transcriptomics.
A working knowledge of immunology, neuroimmunology or inflammatory mechanisms relevant to multiple sclerosis.
Previous experience analysing brain tissue sections or MRI data to investigate brain pathology and structural changes associated with multiple sclerosis specifically.
Programming or data-analysis skills (E.g., R or MATLAB).
Previous experience in a patient-facing or clinical research role in which communicating risk and uncertainty appropriately to participants and families was an important responsibility.
Previous experience working in a research environment with an understanding of research ethics, governance, confidentiality and data protection, and maintenance of accurate laboratory records, sample tracking and research documentation.

Desirable criteria

Experience contributing to publications.
Experience working within a clinical trial with regards to recruitment, engagement, obtaining data (samples/MRIs) and longitudinal follow up.

 We are seeking an experienced Senior Postdoctoral Researcher to lead a defined laboratory-based workstream within the Translational Neuropathology Group (TNG) led by Professor Laura Parkkinen, in the Nuffield Department of Clinical Neurosciences (NDCN), University of Oxford. The role contributes to “Deciphering the Aggregatome: Unravelling Alpha-Synuclein Seeding Drivers in Parkinson’s Disease”, an international research programme supported by Aligning Science Across Parkinson’s (ASAP). The project brings together Oxford, the Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry and LMU Munich.  

 Misfolded α-synuclein aggregates are a defining pathological feature of Parkinson’s disease and related synucleinopathies. Seed amplification assays (SAAs), including RT-QuIC, can detect disease-associated α-synuclein seeding activity in human samples. The TNG group in Oxford has contributed to the development and application of these approaches in cerebrospinal fluid [1, 2] and to the biochemical characterisation of human brain-derived α-synuclein aggregates [3]. However, it remains unclear which molecular features explain differences in seeding activity and clinical progression.

 The collaborative project will investigate the “aggregatome”, the molecular environment associated with α-synuclein aggregates, including interacting proteins, post-translational modifications, lipids and glycosaminoglycans. Complementary SAAs will be combined with biochemical and structural analyses, spatially resolved measurements and multi-omics data across brain tissue, cerebrospinal fluid, blood and skin. By comparing matched and longitudinal samples, the consortium aims to distinguish factors associated with seeding from those that functionally modify it, and to identify potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

 Reporting to Professor Laura Parkkinen, the postholder will lead the Oxford research workstream focused on the measurement, mechanistic investigation and interpretation of α-synuclein seeding activity across human brain tissue and biofluids. They will independently develop research questions and experimental strategies within the agreed programme, supervise junior researchers, coordinate specialist laboratory activities and manage resources allocated to their workstream.

 The postholder will establish and critically evaluate quantitative, recursive and in situ seed amplification assays [4-6]; integrate kinetic results with biochemical, structural, spatial and multi-omics findings; and lead high-quality scientific outputs. They will collaborate closely with the ASAP network, contribute to grant development and project reporting, and ensure rigorous research governance, reproducibility and timely open-science sharing, subject to consent and data-access requirements.

 We are seeking a Research Assistant to the Translational Neuropathology Group (TNG) led by Professor Laura Parkkinen, in the Nuffield Department of Clinical Neurosciences (NDCN), University of Oxford. The post is part of “Deciphering the Aggregatome: Unravelling Alpha-Synuclein Seeding Drivers in Parkinson’s Disease”, an international research programme supported by Aligning Science Across Parkinson’s (ASAP). The project brings together Oxford, the Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry and LMU Munich to investigate why Parkinson’s disease progresses differently between individuals and to identify molecular determinants of α-synuclein seeding.

 Misfolded α-synuclein aggregates are a defining pathological feature of Parkinson’s disease and related synucleinopathies. Seed amplification assays (SAAs), including RT-QuIC, can detect disease-associated α-synuclein seeding activity in human samples. The TNG group in Oxford has contributed to the development and application of these approaches in cerebrospinal fluid [1, 2] and to the biochemical characterisation of human brain-derived α-synuclein aggregates [3]. However, it remains unclear which molecular features explain differences in seeding activity and clinical progression.

 The collaborative project will investigate the “aggregatome”, the molecular environment associated with α-synuclein aggregates, including interacting proteins, post-translational modifications, lipids and glycosaminoglycans. Complementary SAAs will be combined with biochemical and structural analyses, spatially resolved measurements and multi-omics data across brain tissue, cerebrospinal fluid, blood and skin. By comparing matched and longitudinal samples, the consortium aims to distinguish factors associated with seeding from those that functionally modify it, and to identify potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

 At Oxford, the postholder will contribute primarily to the experimental characterisation and quantification of α-synuclein seeding and to the preparation and analysis of human biosamples. Working with Professor Parkkinen and under the day-to-day supervision of Dr Livia Civitelli, they will collaborate with scientists in Oxford and across the ASAP Collaborative Research Network. This is an opportunity to develop specialist skills in translational neuropathology, quantitative assays, reproducible data analysis and open science within a multidisciplinary international programme.

 The postholder will optimise, perform and quality-control α-synuclein SAAs on cerebrospinal fluid and brain-derived material, and, as required by the study plan, other human biomaterials. They will support complementary assay formats, including quantitative, recursive and in situ approaches [4-6], where appropriate to their training and project priorities; compare assay kinetics and seeding profiles; and assist with biochemical and morphological characterisation of native and amplified aggregates. They will maintain rigorous sample traceability, experimental records and reproducible analysis workflows, and contribute data and protocols to consortium-wide analyses and outputs.

 This Clinical Research Fellow role involves supporting hepatology and metabolic disease research, with a focus on metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and chronic hepatitis B (HBV). Key duties include recruiting and assessing patients for research studies and clinical trials, collecting and analysing clinical data, maintaining accurate research records, and contributing to the development of research projects. Job Title:  Research Associate
Posting Start Date:  03/11/2026

School/Department:  School of Medicine & Population Health
Work Arrangement:  Part Time (Hybrid)
Contract Type:  Fixed-term
Salary per annum (£):  39,560.00
Closing Date:  17/11/2026

The University of Sheffield is a remarkable place to work. Our people are at the heart of everything we do. Their diverse backgrounds, abilities and beliefs make Sheffield a world-class university.

 

We offer a fantastic range of benefits including a highly competitive annual leave entitlement (with the ability to purchase more), a generous pensions scheme, flexible working opportunities, a commitment to your development and wellbeing, a wide range of retail discounts, and much more. Find out more about our benefits (opens in a new window) and join us to become part of something special.

 

Overview

 

We are looking to appoint an experienced Research Associate with qualitative and quantitative data analysis skills to join the School of Medicine and Population Health to work on our ‘Delivering Care Closer to Home’ theme as part of the Yorkshire & Humber Applied Research Collaboration. We are seeking an individual with a strong understanding of health psychology and behavioural change who can help to deliver high impact research that can help support the shift of care from hospital to community.

 

 

The candidate will undertake and lead research and consultancy projects, including delivery of existing research projects (evaluation of primary care group clinics, exploring avoidable emergency readmissions). They will also develop and deliver research bids in response to funding calls prioritised by the Department of Health and Social Care and securing additional funding via open research calls or Fellowship applications. The role will have a strong focus on co-production and research inclusion.

 

The post holder will be responsible for developing research protocols, undertaking qualitative interviews and surveys with patients, carers and healthcare providers, conducting qualitative and quantitative analysis and preparing outputs for various audiences (academic, health and social care professionals, and lived experience) . You will have a strong background in co-design and co-production methods, including participatory systems mapping and be a skilled facilitator and listener. Importantly, you will be able to build trust with a wide range of stakeholders and be able to work sensitively with people with lived experience  of a range of conditions and use creative, culturally grounded approaches to involve people meaningfully.

 

Main duties and responsibilities

 

Work closely with team members to undertake a range of research activities, managing daily work from multiple workstreams and multiple research projects.
Lead on organising and conducting fieldwork for projects within the responsive theme of the ARC.  Some travel will be required, mainly within the Yorkshire region.
Lead analysis of qualitative data, supported by senior researchers in the team.
Horizon scan for research funding and respond to research funding calls by developing research grants to support delivery of care closer to home.
Co-ordinate research activity and liaise with members of the research team within the University of Sheffield and partner NHS and social care organisations to ensure delivery of research to study deadlines
Ensure that all research is conducted in accordance with relevant legislation and within the requirements of research ethics and governance, including recruitment of participants and obtaining informed consent.
Contribute to the writing of study reports, conference abstracts and other dissemination materials.
Liaise with existing Patient and Public Involvement and Engagement group and Stakeholder group to ensure emerging findings are shared and discussed.  Expand and support these groups to engage in future research to ensure dissemination activities are inclusive.
Attend team, research group and other section or School meetings as required
You will make a full and active contribution to the principles of the ‘Sheffield Academic’. These include the achievement of excellence in applied teaching and research, and scholarly pursuits to make a genuine difference in the subject area and to the University’s achievements as a whole.
As a member of staff you will be encouraged to make ethical decisions in your role, embedding the University of Sheffield One University strategy into your working activities wherever possible.
Carry out other duties, commensurate with the grade and remit of the post

 

 

Person Specification

 

Our diverse community of staff and students recognises the unique abilities, backgrounds, and beliefs of all. We foster a culture where everyone feels they belong and is respected. Even if your past experience doesn't match perfectly with this role's criteria, your contribution is valuable, and we encourage you to apply. Please ensure that you reference the application criteria in the application statement when you apply.

 The Health Data, MLTC and AI Group (HMAI) is based in the University of Southampton’s Primary Care Research Centre. We combine complex data with AI and clinical expertise to understand health and transform care. Our work spans population health intelligence, digital phenotyping and product innovation — translating research into scalable technologies for more personalised, predictive and preventative healthcare.

 About the role 

 You will contribute to the development and commercialisation of AI-enabled healthcare tools, combining hands-on software engineering and system architecture with product development, evaluation and implementation.

 Working closely with the Chief Investigator and clinical, academic and industry partners, you will design and implement technical architectures connecting diverse datasets, research algorithms, AI components and external services. You will build, test and deploy software, incorporating large language model and agentic AI capabilities where appropriate, and translate clinical and user requirements into practical product features.

 Alongside technical delivery, you will support product planning, commercial partnerships, customer discovery, business models, demonstrations, funding applications and pilot delivery. You will maintain robust engineering workflows and documentation, addressing interoperability, security, governance and responsible AI throughout development.

 The post is part-time (20 hours per week) fixed-term until 30/04/2027, at Level 4 with potential for extension

 About you 

 You will hold a relevant PhD or equivalent professional experience in software engineering, computer science, artificial intelligence or a related discipline.

 Strong programming skills and demonstrable experience of building functioning software are essential. You will have practical experience of system architecture, APIs, databases, testing and deployment, alongside experience of integrating AI into applications.

 You will combine technical rigour with commercial awareness and an interest in translating research into usable products. You will be able to organise development activities, deliver agreed milestones and explain technical decisions clearly to clinical, academic and commercial colleagues.

 Experience of digital health, commercial product development, industry partnerships, customer discovery or university spin-outs would be advantageous. We value collaborative working, user-centred development and a commitment to safe, inclusive and reproducible innovation.

Date: 4 Nov 2026

Location: COVENTRY, GB, CV4 7AL

Company: University of Warwick

Job Title: Research Fellow (112354)

Reference:  502             

Department: Life Sciences

Contract Type: Fixed-term contract

Fixed Term End Date: 28 February 2029

Hours: Full-time (1.0 FTE)

Closing Date: Wednesday 25 November 2026, 11:59 PM (UK)                        

Full time Salary Range: £36,320.00 - £46,970.00 per annum

About the Role

You will join the Bending group/team in the School of Life Sciences at Warwick University.

https://warwick.ac.uk/fac/sci/lifesci/people/gbending/

 

You will undertake research on plant-microbe interactions in the research group of Professor Gary Bending in the School of Life Sciences, working on the European Research Council (ERC) Advanced grant project ‘Rhizosphere Rhythms: Unravelling Diurnal Microbiome Dynamics and Their Role in Plant–Soil Interactions’. You will design and undertake experiments with synthetic bacterial communities to investigate the way in which the plant circadian clock controls rhythmicity of the rhizosphere microbiome via exudation and plant immune responses. You will liaise closely with collaborators in the UK and overseas, and with other research staff working on the project.

 

We and the wider University of Warwick environment offer substantial opportunities for professional development including regular opportunities to attend international conferences.

 

Any requests for further information about the role can be directed to Prof. Gary Bending- gary.bending@warwick.ac.uk

 

For details on the experience and skills required, please refer to the job description (link here).

About You

We are looking for someone with expertise in molecular microbiology, environmental microbiology or plant-microbe interactions.

 

Applicants should be proficient in molecular biology techniques for profiling microbial community composition and abundance, and experience handling synthetic bacterial communities, phages or protists in culture would be an advantage.

 

If you have not yet been awarded your PhD but are near submission or have recently submitted your PhD, any offers of employment will be made as Research Assistant at the top of level 5 within the University grade structure. Upon successful award of your PhD and evidence of this fact, you will be promoted to Research Fellow on the first point of the level 6 of the University grade structure, unless exceptional experience applies to warrant a higher salary.

About the Department

The School of Life Sciences (SLS) is a cohesive, enthusiastic community producing world-class, high-impact bioscience research and teaching within an open, friendly, inclusive and highly collaborative environment.

 

For further information about the School of Life Sciences please see our website at:

http://www2.warwick.ac.uk/fac/sci/lifesci

 

We believe that collegiality, openness, inclusivity and diversity are essential for an excellent research and teaching environment. Our workplace ethic has enabled us to gain the Athena SWAN Silver award. We are dedicated to building a diverse and inclusive workplace and encourage applications from all groups with protected characteristics traditionally under-represented in STEM fields. As part of our ongoing commitment to addressing gender equality under the Athena Swan chartermark, we would particularly encourage and welcome applications from female academics. 

 

In your application, you can also include any career breaks you may have taken (e.g. parental/caring/long-term sick leave, part-time work, secondments) or any periods where you were unable or restricted to work because of the COVID-19 pandemic.

How to Apply

To apply please complete your essential personal details and attach a CV and cover letter on the closing date stated.

 

We will review applications throughout the advertising period and may contact shortlisted candidates before the closing date. We therefore encourage interested applicants to submit their application as early as possible. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early should we receive a sufficient number of suitable applications

 

Please ensure your CV includes your most recent employment experience along with any additional relevant experience and education history.

 

Your cover letter should detail your motivation for applying for the role as well as detailing how you meet the essential and desirable criteria.   

 

The interviews will be held: To Be Confirmed

 

We will provide you with a great range of benefits, which include an attractive pension scheme, a generous holiday allowance plus Christmas closure, excellent learning and development opportunities, and savings on a wide range of products and services. We offer a generous maternity/paternity/adoption/parental leave policy, and onsite childcare facilities.

 

We recognise the importance of a healthy work/life balance and offer you access to flexible working, for more information click here.

 

We are proud to say that we are a Living Wage employer.

 

If you are considering relocating to the UK, read our Relocation Guide to find out more about what Warwick has to offer and what might be involved in the process.

 

Warwick is committed to building an organisation of mutual respect and dignity, promoting a welcoming, diverse, and inclusive working and learning environment.  We recognise that everyone is different in a variety of visible and non-visible ways, and that those differences are to be recognised, respected, and valued.  Where possible, we go beyond legislation to provide a place where everyone can thrive, supporting all staff to achieve their full potential. We aspire to remove economic, social, and cultural barriers that may otherwise prevent people from succeeding.

 

We therefore welcome and encourage applications from all communities regardless of culture, background, age, disability, sex/gender, gender identity or expression, ethnicity, religion/belief, or sexual or romantic orientation. To find out more about our social inclusion work at Warwick visit our webpages here.

 

The University currently holds a Race Equality Charter Bronze Award, Athena Swan Sliver Award and a Disability Smart Bronze Award. Further information on all of the University's Awards and Accreditations can be found here. The University of Warwick is also one of the six founder institutions of the EUTOPIA European University Alliance.
